facts.raw_span: diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels
diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting, along with laboratory findings of hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated C-reactive protein, suggests a severe infection, and the presence of Gram-positive cocci in vessels on tissue Gram staining and small organisms within vasculature on punch biopsy findings supports pneumococcal sepsis.
The CT chest/abdomen showing cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia, along with elevated C-reactive protein, supports the diagnosis of necrotizing pneumonia.

The patient's presentation with purpuric retiform patches on each flank, diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities, and bruises on both flanks, suggests purpura fulminans, a condition characterized by rapid progression of hemorrhagic necrosis of the skin.

The patient's presentation with fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, along with laboratory findings of hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated C-reactive protein, and the presence of Gram-positive cocci in vessels on tissue Gram staining, supports the diagnosis of streptococcal toxic shock syndrome.
The CT chest/abdomen showing areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys suspected to represent renal abscesses supports the diagnosis of renal abscess.
The MRI brain showing multifocal lesions, likely septic emboli, along with the presence of small organisms within vasculature on punch biopsy findings, supports the diagnosis of septic emboli.

rationales.F04: Bruises on both flanks suggest a possible vascular or hemorrhagic component, which is more typical of Purpura fulminans.
rationales.F06: Purpuric retiform patches are highly suggestive of Purpura fulminans, which is characterized by rapid progression of hemorrhagic necrosis.
rationales.F10: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia are highly indicative of a severe pulmonary infection, which is consistent with Pneumococcal sepsis and Necrotizing pneumonia.
rationales.F11: Small organisms within vasculature on punch biopsy findings are highly suggestive of a bacterial infection, which is consistent with Pneumococcal sepsis, Purpura fulminans, and Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome.
rationales.F12: Gram-positive cocci in vessels on tissue Gram staining are highly indicative of a bacterial infection, which is consistent with Pneumococcal sepsis, Purpura fulminans, and Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: Purpuric retiform patches, diffuse papules, and bruises on flanks are characteristic of Purpura fulminans, which explains the skin findings and multi-organ involvement.
